dialect.detail: Standard COBOL-85 with FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE (intrinsic function introduced in COBOL-85 addendum); file path syntax suggests PC/Windows environment, possibly GnuCOBOL or Micro Focus on Windows
evidence: ASSIGN TO UT-SYS-INVFILE with PIC X(60) VALUE 'C:\COBOL'
No COMP-3, no EXEC SQL, no vendor-specific extensions

purpose.domain_detail: Student exercise processing a stock market input file to compute price-to-earnings (P/E) ratios
purpose.summary: Reads stock records from a line-sequential input file containing stock code, name, price per share, and earnings per share. Computes the P/E ratio by dividing price per share by earnings per share. Writes an output sequential file with the original fields plus the current date and computed P/E ratio.

notable_features: ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL for input
File paths hardcoded as C:\COBOL in WORKING-STORAGE
EOF-flag pattern using PIC XXX VALUE 'NO'
DIVIDE ... GIVING for P/E ratio calculation
No COMP-3 or packed decimal usage
verdict.notes: Author and date-written fields present (Derek R Schultz, 2/28/2018). Several typos in comments and variable names (e.g. 'EARININGS', 'EARINGINS', 'copmute', 'reconds'). The date output layout in comments (MMDDYYYY) does not match the record layout order (CUR-DAY, CUR-MONTH, CUR-YEAR = DDMMYYYY). FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE returns an 8-char date as YYYYMMDD, so the mapping to OUT-CUR-DATE fields is also inconsistent with the comment. These are typical student-level oversights.
